    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersLe Vrai gruyère gougèresWarm choux puffs baked with gruyère, nutmeg and black pepperHow to make it125ml water60g butter, diced1/2 tsp salt75g plain flour2 eggs80g gruyère, finely gratednutmeg, a pinch1/4 tsp black pepperHeat the oven to 200°C, line 2 trays and grate the gruyère.Bring the water, butter and salt to the boil. Tip in the flour all at once and beat over the heat for 2 minutes until the dough pulls away from the pan.Tip into a bowl and cool for 5 minutes.Beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy, then 60g of the gruyère, the nutmeg and pepper.Spoon or pipe 20 walnut-sized mounds onto the trays and top with the rest of the cheese.Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden, without opening the oven for the first 15.Serve warm.Zion temple flatbreads with smoked eggplantCharred eggplant whipped with tahini, lemon and garlic, with warm torn flatbreadsHow to make it2 large eggplants3 tbsp tahini1 lemon, juiced1 garlic clove, crushed4 tbsp extra virgin olive oilsalt, to taste1/2 tsp smoked paprika1 tbsp parsley, chopped4 flatbreads or pitasChar the eggplants over a gas flame or under a very hot grill, turning, until black and collapsed.Put them in a bowl, cover with a plate and steam for 10 minutes.Peel off the skin, chop the flesh and drain in a sieve.Mash with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, 2 tbsp of the oil and salt to taste.Warm the flatbreads in a hot dry pan and brush with 1 tbsp of the oil.Spoon the dip into a bowl, drizzle with the last of the oil, dust with smoked paprika and parsley and serve with the torn bread.Escargots in garlic butterCausality. You eat one, then you want another.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsMerovingian's coq au vinChicken braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions, over buttery mashHow to make it8 chicken thigh cutlets, skin on1 tbsp olive oil150g bacon, cut into lardons30g butter, for the sauce12 pickling onions, peeled300g button mushrooms2 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp plain flour1 tbsp tomato paste500ml red wine250ml chicken stock4 thyme sprigs2 bay leavessalt and pepper, to taste1kg floury potatoes60g butter, for the mash100ml milk1 tbsp parsley, choppedSeason the chicken and brown it skin side down in the oil in a large heavy casserole, in batches, then turn and brown the other side. Set aside.Fry the bacon in the same pot until crisp, then add the butter, onions and mushrooms and colour for 8 minutes. Add the garlic for the last minute.Stir in the flour and tomato paste for a minute, then pour in the wine and stock, scraping the base. Add the thyme and bay.Return the chicken skin side up, cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes, then uncover and simmer 10 minutes more to reduce the sauce.Meanwhile peel and chop the potatoes, boil until tender, drain and mash with the butter and warm milk, seasoning with salt.Taste the sauce, season, scatter with parsley and serve over the mash.Persephone's gratin dauphinoisPotatoes baked slow in cream and garlic. Cause and effectHow to make it1.2kg potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced400ml thickened cream200ml full cream milk2 garlic cloves, crushed1/4 tsp ground nutmeg20g butterSlice the potatoes thin and butter a baking dish.Warm the cream and milk with the garlic, nutmeg, salt and pepper.Layer the potatoes in the dish and pour the cream over.Bake at 170°C until tender all the way through and golden.SweetsThe Merovingian's chocolate cakeDense dark chocolate and almond cake under a glossy chocolate ganacheHow to make it200g dark chocolate, chopped, for the cake150g butter4 eggs150g caster sugar50g almond meal30g plain flour2 tbsp cocoa powdersalt, a pinch100g dark chocolate, chopped, for the ganache100ml thickened creamHeat the oven to 170°C and grease and line a 20cm round tin.Melt the chocolate for the cake with the butter in a bowl over simmering water, stirring until smooth.Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale and thick.Fold in the chocolate, then the almond meal, flour, cocoa and salt.Bake for 30 minutes until just set with a slight wobble in the middle.Cool completely in the tin.Bring the cream to a simmer, pour over the ganache chocolate, stand 2 minutes and stir until glossy. Pour over the cake and leave to set.Slice with a hot knife.DrinksMerovingian's kir royaleBlackcurrant liqueur topped with chilled sparkling wine and a blackberryHow to make it60ml crème de cassis750ml dry sparkling wine, chilled4 blackberriesChill 4 flutes in the freezer.Pour 15ml of the cassis into each flute.Top slowly with the sparkling wine.Drop a blackberry into each glass and serve.Glass of aged BordeauxMagnificent wine, says the Merovingian, of the 1959 Haut-Brion.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
